# Perform associations between enterotypes, medication use, and health outcomes

Enterotypes were assigned in `arivale_statins_enterotypes.Rmd`. Now let's merge
some health data and continue our associations. 

## Set up and process data

```{r load.libraries}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(ComplexHeatmap)
library(nnet)
library(networkD3)
library(htmlwidgets)
library(ggpubr)
library(purrr)
library(broom)
library(tidyr)
library(emmeans)
library(ggpubr)
```

```{r read.data}
abx_cohort = read.csv('../data/reharmonized_microbes_clr.csv',
                         colClasses = c(public_client_id = "character"))
```

Factor relevant variables

```{r factor.vars}
# Factor variables
abx_cohort$sex <- factor(abx_cohort$sex)                       # Sex
abx_cohort$statin_binary <- factor(abx_cohort$statin_binary)   # Statin use

abx_cohort$vendor_dashboard <- factor(
  abx_cohort$vendor_dashboard)                                 # Microbiome vendor
abx_cohort$vendor <- factor(abx_cohort$vendor)                 # Clinical chem vendor

abx_cohort$abx_recency <- factor(abx_cohort$abx_recency, 
  levels=c("none", "twelve", "three"))                         # Abx recency

abx_cohort <- abx_cohort %>% mutate(
  abx_year = ifelse(abx_recency == "none", 0, 1)
)

abx_cohort$abx_year <- factor(abx_cohort$abx_year)

abx_cohort <- abx_cohort %>% rename(Bacteroides = Bacteria_Bacteroidetes_Bacteroidia_Bacteroidales_Bacteroidaceae_Bacteroides)
```


For this analysis, we will want to remove those who use blood sugar lowering 
medications and are outliers in HbA1c (in case individuals mistakingly reported 
"no" or just have yet to get a formal diagnosis).

```{r check.glucose.med.users}
table(abx_cohort$meds_blood_sugar)
```

```{r remove.glucose.meds}
abx_cohort_no_gmeds <- abx_cohort %>% filter(meds_blood_sugar == "No")
abx_cohort_no_outliers <- abx_cohort_no_gmeds %>%
  filter(
    is.na(GLYCOHEMOGLOBINA1C) | (
      GLYCOHEMOGLOBINA1C >= (
        quantile(GLYCOHEMOGLOBINA1C, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE) - 1.5 * IQR(GLYCOHEMOGLOBINA1C, na.rm = TRUE)) &
      GLYCOHEMOGLOBINA1C <= (
        quantile(GLYCOHEMOGLOBINA1C, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE) + 1.5 * IQR(GLYCOHEMOGLOBINA1C, na.rm = TRUE))
    )
  )
```


```{r}
table(abx_cohort_no_outliers$abx_year, abx_cohort_no_outliers$statin_binary)
```
```{r bacteroides.reg}
bac_clr_reg_statins <- lm(Bacteroides ~
    age + sex + centered_eGFR + vendor_dashboard + 
    PC1 + PC2 + PC3 + PC4 + PC5 + BMI_CALC +
    abx_recency*statin_binary,
  data = abx_cohort_no_outliers)

summary(bac_clr_reg_statins)
```


```{r ldl.reg}
LDL_reg <- lm(LDL_CHOLCALCULATION ~
    age + sex + centered_eGFR + vendor_dashboard + 
    PC1 + PC2 + PC3 + PC4 + PC5 + BMI_CALC + 
      Bacteroides*abx_year*statin_binary,
  data = abx_cohort_no_outliers)

summary(LDL_reg)
```

# Let's add HMG data to maybe use at a surrogate for efficacy

```{r}
# Look at HMG instead of LDL to see if that's a better marker of efficacy
mets <- read.csv("../data/metabolites_merged_used_for_regressions.csv",
                 colClasses = c(public_client_id = "character"))

hmg_df <- mets[, c("public_client_id", "metabolite_112")] # 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutarate

abx_cohort_hmg <- merge(abx_cohort_no_outliers, hmg_df, by = "public_client_id")

# One pooled model with the interaction
hmg_int <- lm(metabolite_112 ~
    age + sex + centered_eGFR + vendor_dashboard +
    PC1 + PC2 + PC3 + PC4 + PC5 + BMI_CALC +
    Bacteroides*abx_year*statin_binary,
  data = abx_cohort_hmg)

summary(hmg_int)
```
Look at relationship between LDL and biomarker

```{r ldl.hmg.plot}
ggplot(
  abx_cohort_hmg,
  aes(
    metabolite_112,
    LDL_CHOLCALCULATION)) +
  geom_jitter() +
  labs(title = "HMG effect on LDL split by statin use") +
  geom_smooth(method="lm") +
  facet_wrap(vars(statin_binary)) +
  stat_cor(method = "spearman")
```


```{r hba1c.reg}
hba1c_reg <- lm(GLYCOHEMOGLOBINA1C ~
    age + sex + centered_eGFR + vendor_dashboard + vendor + 
    PC1 + PC2 + PC3 + PC4 + PC5 + BMI_CALC + Bacteroides*statin_binary*abx_year,
  data = abx_cohort_no_outliers)

summary(hba1c_reg)
```

```{r plot.hba1c}
ggplot(
  abx_cohort_no_outliers,
  aes(
    Bacteroides,
    GLYCOHEMOGLOBINA1C,
    color=abx_year)
  ) +
  geom_jitter() +
  geom_smooth(method="lm") +
  facet_wrap(vars(statin_binary)) +
  stat_cor(method = "spearman")
```

Hypothesis: abx should make both off and on targets more extreme
but perhaps they just make off targets worse? Or is that just a correlate of being
sick?

```{r}
# Look at LDL
ggplot(
  abx_cohort_no_outliers,
  aes(
    Bacteroides,
    LDL_CHOLCALCULATION, 
    color=abx_year)
  ) +
  geom_jitter() +
  geom_smooth(method="lm") +
  facet_wrap(vars(statin_binary)) +
  stat_cor(method = "spearman")
```

# What about re-creating ribbon plot with Bacteroides counts


```{r create.med.context}
# This will paste the text along with the variable condition
# None will be -
# Users will be +
abx_cohort$med_context <- paste0(
  "abx ", ifelse(abx_cohort$abx_recency == "none", "-", "+"), " / ",
  "statin ", ifelse(abx_cohort$statin_binary == 1, "+", "-")
)

abx_cohort$med_context <- factor(abx_cohort$med_context)
```


```{r recreate.ribbon.plot.bac.counts.entero}
set.seed(42) # abx_entero_labs_bac_hmg

ent_levels <- levels(abx_entero_labs_bac_hmg$enterotype)

# We predict enterotype probabilities across BMI
fit <- multinom(enterotype ~ bacteroides_counts_rarefied,
                data = abx_entero_labs_bac_hmg, trace = FALSE)

# Make our grid represent BMI values we have
grid <- data.frame(bacteroides_counts_rarefied = seq(
  min(abx_entero_labs_bac_hmg$bacteroides_counts_rarefied),
  max(abx_entero_labs_bac_hmg$bacteroides_counts_rarefied),
  length.out = 100))

# Compute probabilies
pp <- as.data.frame(
  predict(fit, newdata = grid, type = "probs")
  )[, ent_levels]

cum  <- t(apply(pp, 1, cumsum))

ribbon <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(ent_levels), function(i) {
  data.frame(x = grid$bacteroides_counts_rarefied,
             ymin = if (i == 1) 0 else cum[, i-1],
             ymax = cum[, i],
             enterotype = ent_levels[i])
}))

ribbon$enterotype <- factor(ribbon$enterotype, levels = ent_levels)

band_y <- function(xval, et) {
  sub <- ribbon[ribbon$enterotype == et, ]
  i   <- which.min(abs(sub$x - xval))
  runif(1, sub$ymin[i] + 0.01, sub$ymax[i] - 0.01)
}

abx_entero_labs_bac_hmg$y <- mapply(
  band_y,
  abx_entero_labs_bac_hmg$bacteroides_counts_rarefied,
  as.character(abx_entero_labs_bac_hmg$enterotype))

ent_fills  <- c("Prev"="yellowgreen","Rum"="#FAD7A0","Bac1"="#91c4bf","Bac2"="thistle")
ent_points <- c("Prev"="#1E8449","Rum"="#E67E22","Bac1"="#088888","Bac2"="#A280AE")

# make sure factor levels match in BOTH frames
ribbon$enterotype <- factor(ribbon$enterotype, levels = ent_levels)
abx_entero_labs_bac_hmg$enterotype <- factor(abx_entero_labs_bac_hmg$enterotype,
                                           levels = ent_levels)

ggplot() +
  # layer 1: the fitted bands (800-row grid df)
  geom_ribbon(data = ribbon,
              aes(x = x, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax, fill = enterotype),
              alpha = 0.55) +
  # layer 2: your actual subjects (1666-row df)
  geom_point(data = abx_entero_labs_bac_hmg,
             aes(x = bacteroides_counts_rarefied, y = y, colour = enterotype),
             size = 1.3, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_fill_manual("Enterotypes:", values = ent_fills, breaks = rev(ent_levels)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = ent_points, guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous("Enterotype prevalence (stacked)",
                     limits = c(0,1), breaks = seq(0,1,0.2), expand = c(0,0)) +
  scale_x_continuous("Bacteroides Counts Rarefied") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12)
```
